title: Finite field fibres and quasi-finiteness along a fibre
statement: Algebraic spaces use [def-trf-algebraic-space], schemes use [def-pc-scheme], and universes use [def-weil-size-convention]. Their point spaces have the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]; fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Locally of finite type is tested on etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For a map $h:E\to T$ to a scheme, quasi-finite at $x\in|E|$ means that for every representable etale scheme chart $U\to E$ and every $u\in U$ above $x$, the scheme map $U\to T$ is quasi-finite at $u$ [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Let $S$ be a scheme, $E$ an algebraic space over $S$, and $h:E\to S$ separated and of finite type. Here separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion on every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion], and finite type means quasi-compact and locally of finite type; quasi-compact means that inverse images of quasi-compact opens are quasi-compact. For $s\in S$ and any field extension $K/\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-field], put $E_K=E\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$. The following are equivalent: (i) $|E_K|$ is finite; (ii) $h$ is quasi-finite at every point of $|E|$ over $s$. The equivalence holds for every such $K$, so finiteness for one representative field is equivalent to finiteness for every representative field, including $\kappa(s)$ and its algebraic closures. Empty fibres are included.

proof.text: Fix $s$ and $K/\kappa(s)$, and write $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to S$, $E_K=E\times_S\operatorname{Spec}K$, $p:E_K\to E$ and $h_K:E_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$. The finite-type base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-stack-finite-type-calculus], including its agreement with the ordinary algebraic-space notion, makes $h_K$ of finite type. The separated base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition] makes $h_K$ separated. Quasi-compactness of $E_K$ itself, in the sense of a surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme: $a$ factors through an affine open $V\ni s$ of $S$, and $E_V=E\times_SV=h^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact by the hypothesis on $h$, so there is a surjective etale map $U_0\to E_V$ from a quasi-compact scheme. Since $E_K=E_V\times_V\operatorname{Spec}K$, [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] makes $U=U_0\times_{E_V}E_K=U_0\times_V\operatorname{Spec}K$ a scheme with a surjective etale map $U\to E_K$, and $U$ is quasi-compact, being covered by the finitely many affine schemes $W_i\times_V\operatorname{Spec}K$ for a finite affine open cover $\{W_i\}$ of $U_0$. Thus the field-space criterion below applies to $E_K$ with all its hypotheses.

proof.text: The point-space fibre-product assertion of [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus] gives $\operatorname{im}|p|=|h|^{-1}(\operatorname{im}|a|)=h^{-1}(\{s\})$: the spectrum of the field $K$ has just one point, whose image is $s$. Therefore every point of $E$ over $s$ has a point above it in $E_K$. By the base-change clause of [lem-sfb-space-quasifinite-locus-open], applied to $S'=\operatorname{Spec}K$, the quasi-finite locus of $h_K$ is the inverse image under $|p|$ of the quasi-finite locus of $h$; so $h_K$ is quasi-finite at $z$ exactly when $h$ is quasi-finite at $p(z)$. Surjectivity onto this fibre now gives: $h_K$ is locally quasi-finite if and only if $h$ is quasi-finite at every point over $s$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-field-discreteness-criterion] to the algebraic space $E_K$ over $S$ with the morphism $h_K:E_K\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, which is locally of finite type and separated by step 1. If $|E_K|$ is finite it is discrete and hence $h_K$ is locally quasi-finite. Step 2 then gives quasi-finiteness of $h$ at every point over $s$. Conversely, that quasi-finiteness makes $h_K$ locally quasi-finite by step 2, and the same field-space criterion makes $|E_K|$ discrete.

proof.text: By step 1, $E_K$ admits a surjective etale map $U\to E_K$ from a quasi-compact scheme. Its point map is continuous and surjective by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Given an open cover of $|E_K|$, pull it back to $U$, take a finite subcover, and use surjectivity to obtain a finite subcover of $|E_K|$. If $|E_K|$ is discrete, its cover by all singletons therefore has a finite subcover, so $|E_K|$ is finite. This proves the reverse implication left in step 3. The argument applies to every $K/\kappa(s)$, while condition (ii) does not depend on $K$; hence all the claimed field choices are equivalent. An empty fibre has no points to check and its empty singleton cover is already finite.
